2.text: than usual, Kotelnikoff decided to give his youngest daughter, a girl thirteen

3.text: years old, in marriage to Attowaˊk, the eldest son of Ataˊto, a big man of

4.text: some twenty-five years. He did so, and in exchange for the girl he received

5.text: four slaughtered reindeer. The Chukchee are fond of “alien” women, especially

6.text: of Russian women, and the marriage was decided upon. It was to be cele-

7.text: brated on the morning after the purchase had been made, according to the

8.text: Chukchee ritual, but during the night the bridegroom tried to take his future

9.text: rights by force. The girl, who had wept the whole previous day, screamed

10.text: and called for help. In the camp were two political exiles, who had come

11.text: to buy reindeer-meat for the exiles of the Lower Kolyma. One of them was

12.text: aroused by the screams of the girl, and through his energetic intervention she

13.text: was rescued from the hands of the Chukchee and taken back to the Kolyma.

14.text: The bridegroom threatened vengeance, but nothing further happened. A few

15.text: years later the girl was married to a Russian of the Kolyma.

16.text: Another case of the kind occurred in my presence in the year 1894 in

17.text: the camp of Qerg̣uˊwg̣i the Lame, on the river Omolon. Qerg̣uˊwg̣i belonged

18.text: to a rich family, that owned several large herds. Though lame in one leg,

19.text: he tended his own herd with the help of two herdsmen. Other members of

20.text: the family also had poor neighbors in their camp who assisted them in attending

21.text: to the herd. One of them, Keuteˊhɪn by name, took his daughter to the camp

22.text: of Qerg̣uˊwg̣i and left her for a while in the tent of one of Qerg̣uˊwg̣i’s neigh-

23.text: bors. The girl was about fifteen years old and very pretty, even from the

24.text: point of view of the white man. As soon as her father was away, the lame

25.text: master sent for her, and after a short conversation made her, then and there,

26.text: his second wife. His first wife was older than he. He had married her when

28.text: A few days afterward I met the father of the girl in another camp. He

29.text: called the lame man all sorts of names, and said that in two days he would

30.text: go to settle the account. I returned to the camp of Qerg̣uˊwg̣i to see what

31.text: would follow. Keuteˊhɪn really came, and immediately afterwards entered the

32.text: sleeping-room of the lame man, who did not feel very well and kept to the

33.text: sleeping-room all day. I entered behind the angry father; but nothing unusual

34.text: happened. “I have come for my daughter!” said Keuteˊhɪn, with an angry

35.text: look. “Eh, eh!” answered Qerg̣uˊwg̣i, acknowledging the demand. “Let her

36.text: make her bundle and go with you.” — “I will take that girl with me,” repeated

37.text: the father in the same irascible tone. “Take a couple of young reindeer with

38.text: you.” Nothing more was said. Keuteˊhɪn took the girl and the reindeer.

39.text: A few months afterwards the girl was again in the camp of Qerg̣uˊwg̣i. This

40.text: time the father consented to leave her there.

41.text: I know of two or three cases of rape against married women. One of

42.text: them led to a quarrel between the offender and the woman’s husband. An-

43.text: other only gave cause to much laughter in the neighborhood. In a third case,
